notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White front plates and yellow rear plates, long or short; some cars carry an extra black mainland plate.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left, like Singapore but unlike Taiwan.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Extremely tall apartment towers everywhere, far taller than in Singapore or Taiwan.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Wall-mounted air conditioners on apartment blocks are very common.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Signs are bilingual, with English beside traditional Chinese characters.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Cylindrical grey lamp posts with a wide base, often with a white sticker.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: No utility poles in cities; rural areas have cylindrical wooden poles, single or double, with meters or transformers.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Striped kerbs are almost never seen, unlike Singapore; grey pedestrian guardrails are common.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Yellow pedestrian crossings and some yellow box grids at junctions; white centre lines with white or yellow edges, often on concrete roads.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: White rectangular road signs with a thick black outline; give-way signs have a thick red border and bilingual text.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Yellow bollards with a white arrow in a blue circle, flat or cuboid, mark where cars should go.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Bright orange bins stand on sidewalks; most fire hydrants are red with round tops and three outlets.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Taxis have silver roofs and green bumper stickers; red in the city and Kowloon, green in the north, blue on Lantau.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Mostly double-decker buses, plus minibuses with green or red roofs; Singapore buses are often light green.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Mountainous with green subtropical vegetation; weathered rock walls, often netted, line hillsides. Singapore is flat.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A double-decker tram runs along the north of the main island.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A light rail with green-and-orange platforms and separated tracks serves the northwest.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Crowded gridded streets with older apartments above shops, little glass.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The northwest near the mainland border is flat with waterlogged rice paddies and a big skyline across the border.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Identical apartment blocks facing the same way like a wall, with planted palms along roads.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Peng Chau, Cheung Chau and Lamma have trekker coverage, few cars and narrow streets; Lamma is the hilliest.
